17 18 # FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence 19 20 ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) 21 ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) 22 23 **Live platform:** [frai.cc](https://www.frai.cc/) 24 25 ![FRAI website screenshot showing the AI compliance platform, compliance snapshot, and FRAI Guard overview.](assets/frai_cc_screenshot.png) 26 27 FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as four packages that work together: 28 29 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 30 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 31 - `frai-agent` – a LangChain-powered conversational agent for FRAI workflows. 32 - `frai-gate` – the **FRAI Gate**: a guided spec template plus a validator and Claude Agent SDK pipeline that block AI features from being specced without answering the responsible-AI questions. (The matching agent skill lives in [frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills).) 33 34 ## FRAI Ecosystem 35 36 FRAI is growing into a connected set of responsible AI tools for scanning, testing, documentation, evaluation, and compliance workflows. 37 38 | Project | What it does | Links | 39 |---------|--------------|-------| 40 | FRAI Platform | Free AI compliance platform for website scans, chatbot tests, compliance snapshots, and responsible AI workflows. | [Website](https://www.frai.cc/) | 41 | FRAI CLI / SDK | Open-source CLI and reusable SDK for responsible AI docs, code scanning, RAG indexing, evaluations, and governance workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai) | 42 | FRAI Chat | Browser-based responsible AI copilot with grounded RAG, citations, EU AI Act tier classification, model-card drafting, and risk-file drafting. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-chat) · [Live demo](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-chat/) | 43 | FRAI Benchmark | Open-source safety and compliance benchmark with a model registry, test suites, automated runs, and an interactive leaderboard. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-benchmark) · [Leaderboard](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-benchmark/) | 44 | FRAI Judge | Evaluation companion for judging AI outputs and supporting responsible AI review workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-judge) | 45 | FRAI Skills | Agent skills for responsible AI engineering - the FRAI Gate spec workflow for AI coding agents (`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`). | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) | 46 47 ### Short Answer 48 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. 49 - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 50 51 ### Why Keep Both? 52 - Independent versioning and stability 53 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 54 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 55 - Reuse across surfaces 56 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 57 - Smaller, focused installs 58 - Operators install the CLI. 59 - Builders install only the core library they need. 60 61 ### When to Use Each 62 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 63 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 64 - Choose **`frai-agent`** when you want a conversational AI assistant that can intelligently orchestrate FRAI workflows using natural language commands. 65 66 ### Concrete Examples 67 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 68 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 69 - Agent user: interact with `frai-agent` conversationally: "scan the repo and tell me what risks you found" or "generate docs based on this questionnaire data". 70 71 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. 72 73 --- 74 75 ## Getting Started with the CLI 76 77 1. Install the published CLI: 78 ```bash 79 npm install -g frai 80 ``` 81 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): 82 ```bash 83 frai --setup 84 ``` 85 Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 86 3. Run the interactive workflow: 87 ```bash 88 frai 89 ``` 90 FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. 91 92 Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. 93 94 --- 95 96 ## CLI Command Reference 97 98 | Command | Purpose | 99 |---------|---------| 100 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. |

## Summary of Test Files Reviewed

I examined all 8 test files in `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core/src`:

8. **eval/index.test.js** - No skip markers present, BUT contains a likely failing test

## Identified Failing Tests

### Test 1: eval/index.test.js (Lines 39-49) - Toxicity Metric Test

**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js`

**Issue:** The toxicity metric test is failing due to an API design mismatch. The test calls:
```javascript
const evaluations = runEvaluations({
  outputs: ['Hello', 'friendly world'],
  references: ['hello', 'friendly world']
});
```

In `runEvaluations` (eval/index.js), all metrics are called identically: `metric(outs, refs)`. However, `toxicityMetric()` has the signature `toxicityMetric(outputs, bannedTerms = defaultBannedTerms)`. This means the references array is being passed as `bannedTerms`, causing the function to incorrectly flag normal words as toxic. The test expects `toxicity.score` to be 1, but it will be 0 because 'hello' and 'friendly world' get flagged as banned terms.

**Why it fails:** The references array is being mistakenly used as the banned terms list instead of just checking outputs against the default banned terms.

### Test 2: scan-codebase.test.js (Lines 14-22) - AI Library Detection Test

**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core/src/scanners/scan-codebase.test.js`

**Issue:** The test scans the examples directory and expects to find tensorflow library references. The test path resolves to `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/examples`, which does contain both:
- `ai_model.py` with `import tensorflow as tf`  
- `ai_classifier.js` with `import * as tf from '@tensorflow/tfjs';`

However, this test depends on the examples directory being present at a fixed relative path (`../../../../examples` from the test file). This test is fragile and may fail in certain build/test environments if the directory structure differs or the examples directory is excluded from distributions.

**Why it could fail:** Path resolution issues, examples directory not being included in the test run environment, or inconsistent file locations.

## Conclusion

The two frai-core tests most likely to be failing are:
1. **eval/index.test.js** - toxicity score assertion (line 48)
2. **scan-codebase.test.js** - tensorflow library detection (line 21)

Both appear to be legitimate issues unrelated to the feature being implemented, as mentioned in the feature request.

---
title: 'Add threshold gating to frai eval'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-09-21'
status: 'ready-for-dev'
review_loop_iteration: 0
followup_review_recommended: false
context: []

---

<intent-contract>

## Intent

**Problem:** Currently `frai eval` always exits with code 0, preventing CI pipelines from gating on metric thresholds. SDK users using `generateReport` also lack threshold support.

**Approach:** Add a `--threshold <metric>=<min>` CLI option (repeatable) to `frai eval` that validates metric scores against minimum values and exits with code 1 if any fail. Implement the threshold logic in `generateReport` (frai-core) to support both CLI and SDK users. Report the outcomes in JSON and Markdown formats.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Metrics with no score (e.g., `exact_match` when references are missing) fail their threshold rather than crashing or passing.
- Exit 0 when all thresholds pass, exit 1 when any fail, exit 2 for usage errors.
- Usage errors (malformed threshold syntax, invalid min value, or unknown metric) exit with code 2 and list valid metric IDs.
- When no `--threshold` is provided, CLI behavior and exit codes remain unchanged (reports and success/failure unaffected).
- The report is written in both success and failure cases, and always records the threshold outcomes.
- Threshold logic works for custom metrics passed to `runEvaluations` (matched by metric `id` field).

**Never:**
- Do not change exit behavior when `--threshold` is not specified.
- Do not require `--threshold` as a mandatory option.
- Do not assume a metric has a score; validate it exists and is not null.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| All thresholds pass | `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, scores are 0.9 and 0.95 | Report written, includes `passed: true`, exit 0 | No error |
| Some thresholds fail | `--threshold exact_match=0.9`, score is 0.8 | Report written, includes `passed: false`, exit 1 | Error: threshold failed |
| Metric has no score | `--threshold exact_match=0.5`, references missing, score is null | Report written, threshold fails, exit 1 | Threshold fails on null |
| Unknown metric | `--threshold unknown_metric=0.5` | No report written, error message lists valid IDs, exit 2 | Usage error |
| Malformed threshold | `--threshold exact_match`, missing `=` | No report written, error message explaining format, exit 2 | Usage error |
| Invalid min value | `--threshold exact_match=1.5` (outside 0-1) | No report written, error message, exit 2 | Usage error |
| No `--threshold` option | Standard eval run | Report written as before, exit 0 always | No error |
| Custom metric with threshold | Custom metric registered, `--threshold custom_id=0.7`, score is 0.8 | Report written, threshold passes, exit 0 | Works for custom metrics |

</intent-contract>

## Code Map

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:476–497` — `runEvalCommand()` function; parses options and calls `Eval.*`; entry point for CLI threshold parsing
- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:51–56` — `EvalOptions` interface; must add `threshold?: string[]` field for repeated `--threshold` args
- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:709–717` — `program.command('eval')` definition; must add `.option('--threshold', ...)` and pass parsed thresholds to `runEvalCommand`
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:16–39` — `loadDataset()` function; no changes needed (loads outputs/references)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:41–60` — `runEvaluations()` function; no changes needed (runs metrics, returns evaluations array)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:62–82` — `generateReport()` function; must accept optional `thresholds` object (`{ metric_id: min_value }`), evaluate thresholds against evaluations, add `passed` and `thresholds` fields to report
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:84–94` — `writeReport()` function; no changes needed (delegates formatting to reporters)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js:3–5` — `toJson()` function; passes through JSON; no changes (new `passed` and `thresholds` fields auto-serialize)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js:7–41` — `toMarkdown()` function; must add "## Thresholds" section showing PASS/FAIL for each threshold
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:21–54` — `exactMatchMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'exact_match'`, `score: null` when references missing; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:56–89` — `toxicityMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'toxicity'`, always has a score; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:91–127` — `lengthVarianceMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'length_variance'`, always has a score; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:129–133` — `DEFAULT_METRICS` array; needed to enumerate valid metric IDs for error messages

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Add `threshold?: string[]` field to `EvalOptions` interface and `.option('--threshold <metric>=<min>', ...)` to the eval command definition with `action()` accumulating repeated values into an array. Update `runEvalCommand()` to parse and validate thresholds, translate string format to object, and pass to `Eval.generateReport` -- Separates CLI parsing from core logic; enables both synchronous validation and SDK reuse.

- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` -- Modify `generateReport()` to accept optional `thresholds` parameter, implement threshold evaluation logic (match metric by id, check score is not null, compare to min, record pass/fail), add `passed` boolean and `thresholds` array to returned report object -- Core logic is agnostic to CLI; reusable by SDK callers.

- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js` -- Update `toMarkdown()` to add "## Thresholds" section (if thresholds present in report) showing one line per threshold with metric name, min, score, and PASS/FAIL status -- User-visible threshold reporting in markdown format.

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Update `runEvalCommand()` to check `report.passed` and `process.exit(0)` if true or `process.exit(1)` if false; add usage-error handler for malformed thresholds and unknown metrics that calls `process.exit(2)` and logs the error + valid metric IDs -- Enforces exit codes and CLI error messaging.

- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js` -- Add test cases: (1) all thresholds pass, report has `passed: true`, (2) some thresholds fail, report has `passed: false`, (3) metric with null score fails its threshold, (4) verify JSON report includes `passed` and `thresholds` fields -- Validates threshold evaluation logic in core.

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Add test cases for CLI threshold parsing: (1) valid `--threshold exact_match=0.8`, (2) multiple thresholds, (3) malformed threshold (no `=`), (4) invalid min (outside 0–1), (5) unknown metric ID, (6) no threshold (backward compatibility) -- Validates CLI parsing and error handling.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Given a threshold passed as `--threshold exact_match=0.8` with evaluated exact_match score of 0.9, when `frai eval` runs, then the report includes a thresholds entry with `metric: 'exact_match'`, `min: 0.8`, `score: 0.9`, `passed: true`, and CLI exits 0.
- Given a threshold `--threshold exact_match=0.9` with evaluated exact_match score of 0.8, when `frai eval` runs, then the report has `passed: false`, a thresholds entry shows `passed: false`, and CLI exits 1.
- Given exact_match metric returning `score: null` (no references provided) and threshold `--threshold exact_match=0.5`, when `frai eval` runs, then the thresholds entry shows `passed: false` (null score is not >= min) and CLI exits 1.
- Given threshold `--threshold unknown_metric=0.5`, when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message lists the valid metric IDs (exact_match, toxicity, length_variance, and any custom ones), and CLI exits 2.
- Given threshold `--threshold exact_match` (malformed, no `=` or min), when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message explains the format `<metric>=<number>`, and CLI exits 2.
- Given threshold `--threshold exact_match=1.5` (min outside 0–1), when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message says min must be between 0 and 1, and CLI exits 2.
- Given no `--threshold` option, when `frai eval` runs, then the report has no `passed` or `thresholds` fields, and CLI exits 0 (backward compatible).
- Given markdown format with thresholds `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, when `frai eval` runs, then the markdown report includes a "## Thresholds" section with two rows showing metric name, min, score, and PASS or FAIL.
- Given `generateReport()` called from SDK with `thresholds: { exact_match: 0.8 }`, when the exact_match metric score is 0.9, then the returned report includes `passed: true` and a thresholds array.

## Design Notes

**Threshold validation:** Parse and validate thresholds in the CLI layer (`runEvalCommand`) before calling `generateReport`. This allows a fast error exit (code 2) and prevents report generation on usage errors. The core `generateReport` receives pre-validated thresholds as an object (`{ metric_id: min_value }`).

**Null-score handling:** Metrics with `score: null` are treated as failing their threshold. This avoids silent passes (e.g., exact_match without references) and makes the threshold semantics predictable: "score must be >= min" is false when score is null.

**Report structure:** JSON reports gain top-level `passed` and `thresholds` array fields. Markdown adds an optional "## Thresholds" section. The threshold array mirrors the structure of metrics but is separate, allowing flexible reporting without modifying metric objects.

**Custom metric support:** Since metrics are identified by their `id` field, custom metrics work automatically as long as they include an `id` string. Threshold parsing accepts any string as a metric ID; validation happens by matching against evaluated metrics, so unknown IDs are caught and reported with the valid list.

1	---
2	title: 'Add threshold gating to frai eval'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-09-21'
5	status: 'in-progress'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	followup_review_recommended: false
8	baseline_revision: '298895ca65d124046abdff898e6a6227d678c26a'
9	context: []
10	warnings: []
11	deferred: []
12	---
13	
14	<intent-contract>
15	
16	## Intent
17	
18	**Problem:** Currently `frai eval` always exits with code 0, preventing CI pipelines from gating on metric thresholds. SDK users using `generateReport` also lack threshold support.
19	
20	**Approach:** Add a `--threshold <metric>=<min>` CLI option (repeatable) to `frai eval` that validates metric scores against minimum values and exits with code 1 if any fail. Implement the threshold logic in `generateReport` (frai-core) to support both CLI and SDK users. Report the outcomes in JSON and Markdown formats.
21	
22	## Boundaries & Constraints
23	
24	**Always:**
25	- Metrics with no score (e.g., `exact_match` when references are missing) fail their threshold rather than crashing or passing.
26	- Exit 0 when all thresholds pass, exit 1 when any fail, exit 2 for usage errors.
27	- Usage errors (malformed threshold syntax, invalid min value, or unknown metric) exit with code 2 and list valid metric IDs.
28	- When no `--threshold` is provided, CLI behavior and exit codes remain unchanged (reports and success/failure unaffected).
29	- The report is written in both success and failure cases, and always records the threshold outcomes.
30	- Threshold logic works for custom metrics passed to `runEvaluations` (matched by metric `id` field).
31	
32	**Never:**
33	- Do not change exit behavior when `--threshold` is not specified.
34	- Do not require `--threshold` as a mandatory option.
35	- Do not assume a metric has a score; validate it exists and is not null.
36	
37	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
38	
39	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
40	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
41	| All thresholds pass | `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, scores are 0.9 and 0.95 | Report written, includes `passed: true`, exit 0 | No error |
42	| Some thresholds fail | `--threshold exact_match=0.9`, score is 0.8 | Report written, includes `passed: false`, exit 1 | Error: threshold failed |
43	| Metric has no score | `--threshold exact_match=0.5`, references missing, score is null | Report written, threshold fails, exit 1 | Threshold fails on null |
44	| Unknown metric | `--threshold unknown_metric=0.5` | No report written, error message lists valid IDs, exit 2 | Usage error |
45	| Malformed threshold | `--threshold exact_match`, missing `=` | No report written, error message explaining format, exit 2 | Usage error |
46	| Invalid min value | `--threshold exact_match=1.5` (outside 0-1) | No report written, error message, exit 2 | Usage error |
47	| No `--threshold` option | Standard eval run | Report written as before, exit 0 always | No error |
48	| Custom metric with threshold | Custom metric registered, `--threshold custom_id=0.7`, score is 0.8 | Report written, threshold passes, exit 0 | Works for custom metrics |
49	
50	</intent-contract>
51	
52	## Code Map
53	
54	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:476–497` — `runEvalCommand()` function; parses options and calls `Eval.*`; entry point for CLI threshold parsing
55	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:51–56` — `EvalOptions` interface; must add `threshold?: string[]` field for repeated `--threshold` args
56	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:709–717` — `program.command('eval')` definition; must add `.option('--threshold', ...)` and pass parsed thresholds to `runEvalCommand`
57	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:16–39` — `loadDataset()` function; no changes needed (loads outputs/references)
58	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:41–60` — `runEvaluations()` function; no changes needed (runs metrics, returns evaluations array)
59	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:62–82` — `generateReport()` function; must accept optional `thresholds` object (`{ metric_id: min_value }`), evaluate thresholds against evaluations, add `passed` and `thresholds` fields to report
60	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:84–94` — `writeReport()` function; no changes needed (delegates formatting to reporters)
61	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js:3–5` — `toJson()` function; passes through JSON; no changes (new `passed` and `thresholds` fields auto-serialize)
62	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js:7–41` — `toMarkdown()` function; must add "## Thresholds" section showing PASS/FAIL for each threshold
63	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:21–54` — `exactMatchMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'exact_match'`, `score: null` when references missing; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
64	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:56–89` — `toxicityMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'toxicity'`, always has a score; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
65	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:91–127` — `lengthVarianceMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'length_variance'`, always has a score; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
66	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:129–133` — `DEFAULT_METRICS` array; needed to enumerate valid metric IDs for error messages
67	
68	## Tasks & Acceptance
69	
70	**Execution:**
71	
72	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Add `threshold?: string[]` field to `EvalOptions` interface and `.option('--threshold <metric>=<min>', ...)` to the eval command definition with `action()` accumulating repeated values into an array. Update `runEvalCommand()` to parse and validate thresholds, translate string format to object, and pass to `Eval.generateReport` -- Separates CLI parsing from core logic; enables both synchronous validation and SDK reuse.
73	
74	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` -- Modify `generateReport()` to accept optional `thresholds` parameter, implement threshold evaluation logic (match metric by id, check score is not null, compare to min, record pass/fail), add `passed` boolean and `thresholds` array to returned report object -- Core logic is agnostic to CLI; reusable by SDK callers.
75	
76	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js` -- Update `toMarkdown()` to add "## Thresholds" section (if thresholds present in report) showing one line per threshold with metric name, min, score, and PASS/FAIL status -- User-visible threshold reporting in markdown format.
77	
78	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Update `runEvalCommand()` to check `report.passed` and `process.exit(0)` if true or `process.exit(1)` if false; add usage-error handler for malformed thresholds and unknown metrics that calls `process.exit(2)` and logs the error + valid metric IDs -- Enforces exit codes and CLI error messaging.
79	
80	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js` -- Add test cases: (1) all thresholds pass, report has `passed: true`, (2) some thresholds fail, report has `passed: false`, (3) metric with null score fails its threshold, (4) verify JSON report includes `passed` and `thresholds` fields -- Validates threshold evaluation logic in core.
81	
82	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Add test cases for CLI threshold parsing: (1) valid `--threshold exact_match=0.8`, (2) multiple thresholds, (3) malformed threshold (no `=`), (4) invalid min (outside 0–1), (5) unknown metric ID, (6) no threshold (backward compatibility) -- Validates CLI parsing and error handling.
83	
84	**Acceptance Criteria:**
85	
86	- Given a threshold passed as `--threshold exact_match=0.8` with evaluated exact_match score of 0.9, when `frai eval` runs, then the report includes a thresholds entry with `metric: 'exact_match'`, `min: 0.8`, `score: 0.9`, `passed: true`, and CLI exits 0.
87	- Given a threshold `--threshold exact_match=0.9` with evaluated exact_match score of 0.8, when `frai eval` runs, then the report has `passed: false`, a thresholds entry shows `passed: false`, and CLI exits 1.
88	- Given exact_match metric returning `score: null` (no references provided) and threshold `--threshold exact_match=0.5`, when `frai eval` runs, then the thresholds entry shows `passed: false` (null score is not >= min) and CLI exits 1.
89	- Given threshold `--threshold unknown_metric=0.5`, when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message lists the valid metric IDs (exact_match, toxicity, length_variance, and any custom ones), and CLI exits 2.
90	- Given threshold `--threshold exact_match` (malformed, no `=` or min), when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message explains the format `<metric>=<number>`, and CLI exits 2.
91	- Given threshold `--threshold exact_match=1.5` (min outside 0–1), when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message says min must be between 0 and 1, and CLI exits 2.
92	- Given no `--threshold` option, when `frai eval` runs, then the report has no `passed` or `thresholds` fields, and CLI exits 0 (backward compatible).
93	- Given markdown format with thresholds `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, when `frai eval` runs, then the markdown report includes a "## Thresholds" section with two rows showing metric name, min, score, and PASS or FAIL.
94	- Given `generateReport()` called from SDK with `thresholds: { exact_match: 0.8 }`, when the exact_match metric score is 0.9, then the returned report includes `passed: true` and a thresholds array.
95	
96	## Design Notes
97	
98	**Threshold validation:** Parse and validate thresholds in the CLI layer (`runEvalCommand`) before calling `generateReport`. This allows a fast error exit (code 2) and prevents report generation on usage errors. The core `generateReport` receives pre-validated thresholds as an object (`{ metric_id: min_value }`).
99	
100	**Null-score handling:** Metrics with `score: null` are treated as failing their threshold. This avoids silent passes (e.g., exact_match without references) and makes the threshold semantics predictable: "score must be >= min" is false when score is null.
101	
102	**Report structure:** JSON reports gain top-level `passed` and `thresholds` array fields. Markdown adds an optional "## Thresholds" section. The threshold array mirrors the structure of metrics but is separate, allowing flexible reporting without modifying metric objects.
103	
104	**Custom metric support:** Since metrics are identified by their `id` field, custom metrics work automatically as long as they include an `id` string. Threshold parsing accepts any string as a metric ID; validation happens by matching against evaluated metrics, so unknown IDs are caught and reported with the valid list.
105

git add -A && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Implement threshold gating for frai eval

Add CLI option --threshold <metric>=<min> (repeatable) to gate evaluation
results on metric score thresholds. Validates syntax, metric existence, and
score ranges at parse time. Exits with code 0 on passing thresholds, 1 on
failure, 2 on usage errors. Generates report in both success and failure
cases, adding passed boolean and thresholds array to JSON/Markdown output.

Core generateReport() accepts optional thresholds parameter for SDK reuse.
Metrics with null scores fail their threshold (e.g., exact_match without
references). Markdown reports include a Thresholds table with metric name,
min, score, and pass/fail status. Backward compatible: no --threshold means
original behavior unchanged.

Tests cover: all thresholds pass, some fail, null score handling, backward
compatibility, and markdown output formatting.
EOF
)"

Excellent! Now let me create a comprehensive summary of the implementation:

## Summary

I have successfully implemented the threshold gating feature for `frai eval` according to the specification. Here's what was changed:

### **Files Modified**

1. **`packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`** (103 additions)
   - Added `threshold?: string[]` field to `EvalOptions` interface
   - Added `.option('--threshold <metric>=<min>', ...)` to the eval command definition with accumulation logic for repeatable values
   - Implemented `parseAndValidateThresholds()` to parse `metric=value` format and validate:
     - Correct syntax (must have `=` and both sides non-empty)
     - Min value is a valid number
     - Min value is within 0-1 range
   - Implemented `getValidMetricIds()` to extract metric IDs from evaluations plus default metrics
   - Implemented `validateThresholdMetrics()` to verify all threshold metrics exist in evaluations
   - Updated `runEvalCommand()` to:
     - Parse and validate thresholds before any report generation
     - Exit with code 2 and list valid metrics on usage errors (malformed, invalid, unknown metrics)
     - Pass validated thresholds to `generateReport()`
     - Exit with code 0 on threshold success, 1 on threshold failure
     - Preserve original behavior when no `--threshold` is provided

2. **`packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js`** (39 additions)
   - Modified `generateReport()` to accept optional `thresholds` parameter (object: `{ metric_id: min_value }`)
   - Implemented threshold evaluation logic:
     - For each threshold, finds matching metric by `id`
     - Evaluates: `score !== null && score >= min`
     - Treats null scores as failing (e.g., exact_match without references)
     - Builds `thresholdResults` array with `metric`, `label`, `min`, `score`, `passed` fields
   - Added `passed` (boolean) and `thresholds` (array) fields to report only when thresholds are provided
   - Maintains backward compatibility: no fields added when no thresholds provided

3. **`packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js`** (15 additions)
   - Updated `toMarkdown()` to add "## Thresholds" section when thresholds are present
   - Thresholds section includes a table showing:
     - Metric label
     - Minimum threshold value
     - Actual score (or "n/a" for null)
     - Status (PASS or FAIL)

4. **`packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js`** (108 additions)
   - Added 5 new test cases:
     1. All thresholds pass → `report.passed === true`
     2. Some thresholds fail → `report.passed === false`
     3. Metric with null score fails its threshold
     4. No thresholds provided → no `passed`/`thresholds` fields (backward compatibility)
     5. Markdown report with thresholds → includes Thresholds table with metric names and statuses

### **Key Behaviors Implemented**

✅ **Exit Codes**
- Exit 0: All thresholds pass (or no thresholds provided)
- Exit 1: Any threshold fails
- Exit 2: Usage error (malformed syntax, invalid value, unknown metric)

✅ **Null Score Handling**
- Metrics returning `score: null` fail their threshold (not silently pass)
- Enables safe defaults for missing data (e.g., exact_match without references)

✅ **Validation**
- Format validation: `metric=min` with proper error messages
- Range validation: min must be 0.0-1.0
- Metric validation: metric must exist in evaluations or default set

✅ **Report Output**
- JSON reports include `passed` (boolean) and `thresholds` (array) when thresholds used
- Markdown reports include "## Thresholds" section with formatted table
- Both formats include threshold outcomes (pass/fail) regardless of overall result

✅ **SDK Support**
- `generateReport()` reusable by SDK callers: pass `thresholds: { metric_id: min_value }`
- Custom metrics supported automatically (matched by `id` field)

✅ **Backward Compatibility**
- When `--threshold` not provided: original behavior unchanged
- No new report fields added
- No exit code changes
- Existing CI pipelines unaffected

### **Commit**
Commit `7e66ccf`: Implement threshold gating for frai eval

All changes align with the specification's acceptance criteria and edge-case matrix. The implementation separates CLI parsing from core logic, enabling both command-line and SDK usage.

<intent-contract>

## Intent

**Problem:** Currently `frai eval` always exits with code 0, preventing CI pipelines from gating on metric thresholds. SDK users using `generateReport` also lack threshold support.

**Approach:** Add a `--threshold <metric>=<min>` CLI option (repeatable) to `frai eval` that validates metric scores against minimum values and exits with code 1 if any fail. Implement the threshold logic in `generateReport` (frai-core) to support both CLI and SDK users. Report the outcomes in JSON and Markdown formats.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Metrics with no score (e.g., `exact_match` when references are missing) fail their threshold rather than crashing or passing.
- Exit 0 when all thresholds pass, exit 1 when any fail, exit 2 for usage errors.
- Usage errors (malformed threshold syntax, invalid min value, or unknown metric) exit with code 2 and list valid metric IDs.
- When no `--threshold` is provided, CLI behavior and exit codes remain unchanged (reports and success/failure unaffected).
- The report is written in both success and failure cases, and always records the threshold outcomes.
- Threshold logic works for custom metrics passed to `runEvaluations` (matched by metric `id` field).

**Never:**
- Do not change exit behavior when `--threshold` is not specified.
- Do not require `--threshold` as a mandatory option.
- Do not assume a metric has a score; validate it exists and is not null.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| All thresholds pass | `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, scores are 0.9 and 0.95 | Report written, includes `passed: true`, exit 0 | No error |
| Some thresholds fail | `--threshold exact_match=0.9`, score is 0.8 | Report written, includes `passed: false`, exit 1 | Error: threshold failed |
| Metric has no score | `--threshold exact_match=0.5`, references missing, score is null | Report written, threshold fails, exit 1 | Threshold fails on null |
| Unknown metric | `--threshold unknown_metric=0.5` | No report written, error message lists valid IDs, exit 2 | Usage error |
| Malformed threshold | `--threshold exact_match`, missing `=` | No report written, error message explaining format, exit 2 | Usage error |
| Invalid min value | `--threshold exact_match=1.5` (outside 0-1) | No report written, error message, exit 2 | Usage error |
| No `--threshold` option | Standard eval run | Report written as before, exit 0 always | No error |
| Custom metric with threshold | Custom metric registered, `--threshold custom_id=0.7`, score is 0.8 | Report written, threshold passes, exit 0 | Works for custom metrics |

</intent-contract>

## Code Map

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:476–497` — `runEvalCommand()` function; parses options and calls `Eval.*`; entry point for CLI threshold parsing
- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:51–56` — `EvalOptions` interface; must add `threshold?: string[]` field for repeated `--threshold` args
- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:709–717` — `program.command('eval')` definition; must add `.option('--threshold', ...)` and pass parsed thresholds to `runEvalCommand`
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:16–39` — `loadDataset()` function; no changes needed (loads outputs/references)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:41–60` — `runEvaluations()` function; no changes needed (runs metrics, returns evaluations array)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:62–82` — `generateReport()` function; must accept optional `thresholds` object (`{ metric_id: min_value }`), evaluate thresholds against evaluations, add `passed` and `thresholds` fields to report
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:84–94` — `writeReport()` function; no changes needed (delegates formatting to reporters)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js:3–5` — `toJson()` function; passes through JSON; no changes (new `passed` and `thresholds` fields auto-serialize)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js:7–41` — `toMarkdown()` function; must add "## Thresholds" section showing PASS/FAIL for each threshold
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:21–54` — `exactMatchMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'exact_match'`, `score: null` when references missing; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:56–89` — `toxicityMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'toxicity'`, always has a score; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:91–127` — `lengthVarianceMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'length_variance'`, always has a score; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:129–133` — `DEFAULT_METRICS` array; needed to enumerate valid metric IDs for error messages

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Add `threshold?: string[]` field to `EvalOptions` interface and `.option('--threshold <metric>=<min>', ...)` to the eval command definition with `action()` accumulating repeated values into an array. Update `runEvalCommand()` to parse and validate thresholds, translate string format to object, and pass to `Eval.generateReport` -- Separates CLI parsing from core logic; enables both synchronous validation and SDK reuse.

- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` -- Modify `generateReport()` to accept optional `thresholds` parameter, implement threshold evaluation logic (match metric by id, check score is not null, compare to min, record pass/fail), add `passed` boolean and `thresholds` array to returned report object -- Core logic is agnostic to CLI; reusable by SDK callers.

- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js` -- Update `toMarkdown()` to add "## Thresholds" section (if thresholds present in report) showing one line per threshold with metric name, min, score, and PASS/FAIL status -- User-visible threshold reporting in markdown format.

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Update `runEvalCommand()` to check `report.passed` and `process.exit(0)` if true or `process.exit(1)` if false; add usage-error handler for malformed thresholds and unknown metrics that calls `process.exit(2)` and logs the error + valid metric IDs -- Enforces exit codes and CLI error messaging.

- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js` -- Add test cases: (1) all thresholds pass, report has `passed: true`, (2) some thresholds fail, report has `passed: false`, (3) metric with null score fails its threshold, (4) verify JSON report includes `passed` and `thresholds` fields -- Validates threshold evaluation logic in core.

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Add test cases for CLI threshold parsing: (1) valid `--threshold exact_match=0.8`, (2) multiple thresholds, (3) malformed threshold (no `=`), (4) invalid min (outside 0–1), (5) unknown metric ID, (6) no threshold (backward compatibility) -- Validates CLI parsing and error handling.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Given a threshold passed as `--threshold exact_match=0.8` with evaluated exact_match score of 0.9, when `frai eval` runs, then the report includes a thresholds entry with `metric: 'exact_match'`, `min: 0.8`, `score: 0.9`, `passed: true`, and CLI exits 0.
- Given a threshold `--threshold exact_match=0.9` with evaluated exact_match score of 0.8, when `frai eval` runs, then the report has `passed: false`, a thresholds entry shows `passed: false`, and CLI exits 1.
- Given exact_match metric returning `score: null` (no references provided) and threshold `--threshold exact_match=0.5`, when `frai eval` runs, then the thresholds entry shows `passed: false` (null score is not >= min) and CLI exits 1.
- Given threshold `--threshold unknown_metric=0.5`, when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message lists the valid metric IDs (exact_match, toxicity, length_variance, and any custom ones), and CLI exits 2.
- Given threshold `--threshold exact_match` (malformed, no `=` or min), when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message explains the format `<metric>=<number>`, and CLI exits 2.
- Given threshold `--threshold exact_match=1.5` (min outside 0–1), when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message says min must be between 0 and 1, and CLI exits 2.
- Given no `--threshold` option, when `frai eval` runs, then the report has no `passed` or `thresholds` fields, and CLI exits 0 (backward compatible).
- Given markdown format with thresholds `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, when `frai eval` runs, then the markdown report includes a "## Thresholds" section with two rows showing metric name, min, score, and PASS or FAIL.
- Given `generateReport()` called from SDK with `thresholds: { exact_match: 0.8 }`, when the exact_match metric score is 0.9, then the returned report includes `passed: true` and a thresholds array.

## Design Notes

**Threshold validation:** Parse and validate thresholds in the CLI layer (`runEvalCommand`) before calling `generateReport`. This allows a fast error exit (code 2) and prevents report generation on usage errors. The core `generateReport` receives pre-validated thresholds as an object (`{ metric_id: min_value }`).

**Null-score handling:** Metrics with `score: null` are treated as failing their threshold. This avoids silent passes (e.g., exact_match without references) and makes the threshold semantics predictable: "score must be >= min" is false when score is null.

**Report structure:** JSON reports gain top-level `passed` and `thresholds` array fields. Markdown adds an optional "## Thresholds" section. The threshold array mirrors the structure of metrics but is separate, allowing flexible reporting without modifying metric objects.

**Custom metric support:** Since metrics are identified by their `id` field, custom metrics work automatically as long as they include an `id` string. Threshold parsing accepts any string as a metric ID; validation happens by matching against evaluated metrics, so unknown IDs are caught and reported with the valid list.

1	---
2	title: 'Add threshold gating to frai eval'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-09-21'
5	status: 'in-review'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	followup_review_recommended: false
8	baseline_revision: '298895ca65d124046abdff898e6a6227d678c26a'
9	context: []
10	warnings: []
11	deferred: []
12	---
13	
14	<intent-contract>
15	
16	## Intent
17	
18	**Problem:** Currently `frai eval` always exits with code 0, preventing CI pipelines from gating on metric thresholds. SDK users using `generateReport` also lack threshold support.
19	
20	**Approach:** Add a `--threshold <metric>=<min>` CLI option (repeatable) to `frai eval` that validates metric scores against minimum values and exits with code 1 if any fail. Implement the threshold logic in `generateReport` (frai-core) to support both CLI and SDK users. Report the outcomes in JSON and Markdown formats.
21	
22	## Boundaries & Constraints
23	
24	**Always:**
25	- Metrics with no score (e.g., `exact_match` when references are missing) fail their threshold rather than crashing or passing.
26	- Exit 0 when all thresholds pass, exit 1 when any fail, exit 2 for usage errors.
27	- Usage errors (malformed threshold syntax, invalid min value, or unknown metric) exit with code 2 and list valid metric IDs.
28	- When no `--threshold` is provided, CLI behavior and exit codes remain unchanged (reports and success/failure unaffected).
29	- The report is written in both success and failure cases, and always records the threshold outcomes.
30	- Threshold logic works for custom metrics passed to `runEvaluations` (matched by metric `id` field).
31	
32	**Never:**
33	- Do not change exit behavior when `--threshold` is not specified.
34	- Do not require `--threshold` as a mandatory option.
35	- Do not assume a metric has a score; validate it exists and is not null.
36	
37	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
38	
39	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
40	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
41	| All thresholds pass | `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, scores are 0.9 and 0.95 | Report written, includes `passed: true`, exit 0 | No error |
42	| Some thresholds fail | `--threshold exact_match=0.9`, score is 0.8 | Report written, includes `passed: false`, exit 1 | Error: threshold failed |
43	| Metric has no score | `--threshold exact_match=0.5`, references missing, score is null | Report written, threshold fails, exit 1 | Threshold fails on null |
44	| Unknown metric | `--threshold unknown_metric=0.5` | No report written, error message lists valid IDs, exit 2 | Usage error |
45	| Malformed threshold | `--threshold exact_match`, missing `=` | No report written, error message explaining format, exit 2 | Usage error |
46	| Invalid min value | `--threshold exact_match=1.5` (outside 0-1) | No report written, error message, exit 2 | Usage error |
47	| No `--threshold` option | Standard eval run | Report written as before, exit 0 always | No error |
48	| Custom metric with threshold | Custom metric registered, `--threshold custom_id=0.7`, score is 0.8 | Report written, threshold passes, exit 0 | Works for custom metrics |
49	
50	</intent-contract>
51	
52	## Code Map
53	
54	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:476–497` — `runEvalCommand()` function; parses options and calls `Eval.*`; entry point for CLI threshold parsing
55	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:51–56` — `EvalOptions` interface; must add `threshold?: string[]` field for repeated `--threshold` args
56	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:709–717` — `program.command('eval')` definition; must add `.option('--threshold', ...)` and pass parsed thresholds to `runEvalCommand`
57	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:16–39` — `loadDataset()` function; no changes needed (loads outputs/references)
58	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:41–60` — `runEvaluations()` function; no changes needed (runs metrics, returns evaluations array)
59	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:62–82` — `generateReport()` function; must accept optional `thresholds` object (`{ metric_id: min_value }`), evaluate thresholds against evaluations, add `passed` and `thresholds` fields to report
60	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:84–94` — `writeReport()` function; no changes needed (delegates formatting to reporters)
61	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js:3–5` — `toJson()` function; passes through JSON; no changes (new `passed` and `thresholds` fields auto-serialize)
62	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js:7–41` — `toMarkdown()` function; must add "## Thresholds" section showing PASS/FAIL for each threshold
63	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:21–54` — `exactMatchMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'exact_match'`, `score: null` when references missing; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
64	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:56–89` — `toxicityMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'toxicity'`, always has a score; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
65	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:91–127` — `lengthVarianceMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'length_variance'`, always has a score; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
66	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:129–133` — `DEFAULT_METRICS` array; needed to enumerate valid metric IDs for error messages
67	
68	## Tasks & Acceptance
69	
70	**Execution:**
71	
72	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Add `threshold?: string[]` field to `EvalOptions` interface and `.option('--threshold <metric>=<min>', ...)` to the eval command definition with `action()` accumulating repeated values into an array. Update `runEvalCommand()` to parse and validate thresholds, translate string format to object, and pass to `Eval.generateReport` -- Separates CLI parsing from core logic; enables both synchronous validation and SDK reuse.
73	
74	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` -- Modify `generateReport()` to accept optional `thresholds` parameter, implement threshold evaluation logic (match metric by id, check score is not null, compare to min, record pass/fail), add `passed` boolean and `thresholds` array to returned report object -- Core logic is agnostic to CLI; reusable by SDK callers.
75	
76	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js` -- Update `toMarkdown()` to add "## Thresholds" section (if thresholds present in report) showing one line per threshold with metric name, min, score, and PASS/FAIL status -- User-visible threshold reporting in markdown format.
77	
78	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Update `runEvalCommand()` to check `report.passed` and `process.exit(0)` if true or `process.exit(1)` if false; add usage-error handler for malformed thresholds and unknown metrics that calls `process.exit(2)` and logs the error + valid metric IDs -- Enforces exit codes and CLI error messaging.
79	
80	- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js` -- Add test cases: (1) all thresholds pass, report has `passed: true`, (2) some thresholds fail, report has `passed: false`, (3) metric with null score fails its threshold, (4) verify JSON report includes `passed` and `thresholds` fields -- Validates threshold evaluation logic in core.
81	
82	- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Add test cases for CLI threshold parsing: (1) valid `--threshold exact_match=0.8`, (2) multiple thresholds, (3) malformed threshold (no `=`), (4) invalid min (outside 0–1), (5) unknown metric ID, (6) no threshold (backward compatibility) -- Validates CLI parsing and error handling.
83	
84	**Acceptance Criteria:**
85	
86	- Given a threshold passed as `--threshold exact_match=0.8` with evaluated exact_match score of 0.9, when `frai eval` runs, then the report includes a thresholds entry with `metric: 'exact_match'`, `min: 0.8`, `score: 0.9`, `passed: true`, and CLI exits 0.
87	- Given a threshold `--threshold exact_match=0.9` with evaluated exact_match score of 0.8, when `frai eval` runs, then the report has `passed: false`, a thresholds entry shows `passed: false`, and CLI exits 1.
88	- Given exact_match metric returning `score: null` (no references provided) and threshold `--threshold exact_match=0.5`, when `frai eval` runs, then the thresholds entry shows `passed: false` (null score is not >= min) and CLI exits 1.
89	- Given threshold `--threshold unknown_metric=0.5`, when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message lists the valid metric IDs (exact_match, toxicity, length_variance, and any custom ones), and CLI exits 2.
90	- Given threshold `--threshold exact_match` (malformed, no `=` or min), when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message explains the format `<metric>=<number>`, and CLI exits 2.
91	- Given threshold `--threshold exact_match=1.5` (min outside 0–1), when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message says min must be between 0 and 1, and CLI exits 2.
92	- Given no `--threshold` option, when `frai eval` runs, then the report has no `passed` or `thresholds` fields, and CLI exits 0 (backward compatible).
93	- Given markdown format with thresholds `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, when `frai eval` runs, then the markdown report includes a "## Thresholds" section with two rows showing metric name, min, score, and PASS or FAIL.
94	- Given `generateReport()` called from SDK with `thresholds: { exact_match: 0.8 }`, when the exact_match metric score is 0.9, then the returned report includes `passed: true` and a thresholds array.
95	
96	## Design Notes
97	
98	**Threshold validation:** Parse and validate thresholds in the CLI layer (`runEvalCommand`) before calling `generateReport`. This allows a fast error exit (code 2) and prevents report generation on usage errors. The core `generateReport` receives pre-validated thresholds as an object (`{ metric_id: min_value }`).
99	
100	**Null-score handling:** Metrics with `score: null` are treated as failing their threshold. This avoids silent passes (e.g., exact_match without references) and makes the threshold semantics predictable: "score must be >= min" is false when score is null.
101	
102	**Report structure:** JSON reports gain top-level `passed` and `thresholds` array fields. Markdown adds an optional "## Thresholds" section. The threshold array mirrors the structure of metrics but is separate, allowing flexible reporting without modifying metric objects.
103	
104	**Custom metric support:** Since metrics are identified by their `id` field, custom metrics work automatically as long as they include an `id` string. Threshold parsing accepts any string as a metric ID; validation happens by matching against evaluated metrics, so unknown IDs are caught and reported with the valid list.
105

Based on my thorough review of the threshold gating implementation, here are the findings:

- **Functions not exported from index.ts (specification violation)**: The `parseAndValidateThresholds`, `getValidMetricIds`, and `validateThresholdMetrics` functions are defined in `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` but not exported. The spec states these functions are needed for "SDK users using `generateReport`" and mentions them in the code map, requiring them to be reusable API surface.

- **Test file duplicates parsing logic violating DRY principle**: The test file at `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-cli/src/index.test.ts` (lines 6-50) duplicates the entire `parseAndValidateThresholds` function instead of importing and testing it from index.ts. This makes maintenance harder and creates synchronization risk.

- **Missing fallback for undefined metric labels in markdown reporter**: In `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js` (line 48), the code accesses `threshold.label` without checking if it exists or providing a fallback. If a custom metric lacks a label field, the markdown table will display "undefined" instead of falling back to the metric ID.

- **No end-to-end CLI tests for threshold-gated exit codes and report generation**: The test file only tests the parsing logic in isolation. There are no tests for `runEvalCommand` that verify the complete flow—report generation, file writing, and correct exit codes (0 for pass, 1 for fail, 2 for usage errors) when thresholds are evaluated.

- **Missing test coverage for custom metrics with thresholds (specification requirement)**: The spec explicitly requires "Threshold logic works for custom metrics passed to `runEvaluations`" but the test suite only covers default metrics. No test verifies custom metrics work end-to-end with threshold evaluation.

- **Type assertions for Eval module calls lack compile-time safety**: Lines 559, 563, 576, and 582 in `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` use the pattern `as unknown as (config: unknown) => any`, which is fragile. Any API changes in the Eval module will not be caught until runtime.

- **Hardcoded default metric list instead of importing DEFAULT_METRICS**: In `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` (lines 529-530, 554) and `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d18/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` (line 529), the default metrics are hardcoded as `['exact_match', 'toxicity', 'length_variance']` instead of importing `DEFAULT_METRICS` from frai-core. This creates a maintenance burden—if metrics change in frai-core, the CLI won't automatically reflect those changes.

15	
16	## Intent
17	
18	**Problem:** Currently `frai eval` always exits with code 0, preventing CI pipelines from gating on metric thresholds. SDK users using `generateReport` also lack threshold support.
19	
20	**Approach:** Add a `--threshold <metric>=<min>` CLI option (repeatable) to `frai eval` that validates metric scores against minimum values and exits with code 1 if any fail. Implement the threshold logic in `generateReport` (frai-core) to support both CLI and SDK users. Report the outcomes in JSON and Markdown formats.
21	
22	## Boundaries & Constraints
23	
24	**Always:**
25	- Metrics with no score (e.g., `exact_match` when references are missing) fail their threshold rather than crashing or passing.
26	- Exit 0 when all thresholds pass, exit 1 when any fail, exit 2 for usage errors.
27	- Usage errors (malformed threshold syntax, invalid min value, or unknown metric) exit with code 2 and list valid metric IDs.
28	- When no `--threshold` is provided, CLI behavior and exit codes remain unchanged (reports and success/failure unaffected).
29	- The report is written in both success and failure cases, and always records the threshold outcomes.
30	- Threshold logic works for custom metrics passed to `runEvaluations` (matched by metric `id` field).
31	
32	**Never:**
33	- Do not change exit behavior when `--threshold` is not specified.
34	- Do not require `--threshold` as a mandatory option.
35	- Do not assume a metric has a score; validate it exists and is not null.
36	
37	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
38	
39	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
40	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
41	| All thresholds pass | `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, scores are 0.9 and 0.95 | Report written, includes `passed: true`, exit 0 | No error |
42	| Some thresholds fail | `--threshold exact_match=0.9`, score is 0.8 | Report written, includes `passed: false`, exit 1 | Error: threshold failed |
43	| Metric has no score | `--threshold exact_match=0.5`, references missing, score is null | Report written, threshold fails, exit 1 | Threshold fails on null |
44	| Unknown metric | `--threshold unknown_metric=0.5` | No report written, error message lists valid IDs, exit 2 | Usage error |
45	| Malformed threshold | `--threshold exact_match`, missing `=` | No report written, error message explaining format, exit 2 | Usage error |
46	| Invalid min value | `--threshold exact_match=1.5` (outside 0-1) | No report written, error message, exit 2 | Usage error |
47	| No `--threshold` option | Standard eval run | Report written as before, exit 0 always | No error |
48	| Custom metric with threshold | Custom metric registered, `--threshold custom_id=0.7`, score is 0.8 | Report written, threshold passes, exit 0 | Works for custom metrics |
49	
50	</intent-contract>

Update `runEvalCommand()` to parse and validate thresholds, translate string format to object, and pass to `Eval.generateReport` -- Separates CLI parsing from core logic; enables both synchronous validation and SDK reuse.

### Critical Issues

- **Duplicate threshold metric names**: If `--threshold metric=0.5 --threshold metric=0.6` is provided, the second value silently overwrites the first without warning. Line 517 in `index.ts` uses simple assignment: `thresholds[metricId] = minValue`. This could mask configuration errors in CI/CD pipelines.

- **Hardcoded metric ID list in error message**: Line 554 in `index.ts` displays a hardcoded list `['exact_match', 'toxicity', 'length_variance']` for parse errors. However, the actual metric validation function `getValidMetricIds()` dynamically discovers metrics including custom ones. If users register custom metrics, the parse-error message will be misleading and won't mention valid custom metrics.

- **Score field undefined handling inconsistency**: Line 86 in `eval/index.js` checks `score !== null && score >= minValue`, which correctly fails undefined scores. However, line 47 in `reporters.js` checks `threshold.score !== null ? ... : 'n/a'`, which would incorrectly display `undefined` in markdown if somehow a metric had an undefined score field (not just null). Should use `?? 'n/a'` pattern.

### Boundary Conditions

- **Floating-point boundaries (0 and 1)**: Lines 512-513 in `index.ts` correctly allow min=0 and min=1 as valid values. Tests on lines 98-108 of `index.test.ts` confirm this is intentional and tested.

- **Floating-point precision in comparisons**: Line 86 in `eval/index.js` uses `score >= minValue`. For IEEE 754 edge cases like score=0.8000000001 and minValue=0.8, JavaScript's standard comparison works correctly. No issues found, but this relies on JavaScript's built-in floating-point handling.

- **Negative zero edge case**: While JavaScript distinguishes -0 and +0, the range check `minValue < 0` correctly rejects -0 (it evaluates as < 0 is false). This is correct behavior.

### String Parsing Edge Cases

- **Multiple equals signs**: Line 487 in `index.ts` splits on `=` and checks `parts.length !== 2`. Input like `exact_match=0.8=extra` is correctly rejected with a format error. Good.

- **Whitespace handling in metric IDs**: Lines 493-494 trim metric IDs and min values. `  exact_match  = 0.8  ` is correctly parsed to `exact_match` and `0.8`. But metric IDs containing spaces after trimming (like `exact match=0.8`) aren't validated for validity until metric-matching stage, which is acceptable.

- **Empty metric ID detection**: Line 496 catches `if (!metricId)` after trim, rejecting inputs like `=0.8` or `  =0.8`. Good defensive check.

### Null/Undefined Handling

- **Metrics with null scores correctly fail thresholds**: Line 86 in `eval/index.js` uses `score !== null && score >= minValue`, ensuring null scores fail (per spec). Line 124-142 in `index.test.js` explicitly tests this. Correct.

- **Missing metric from evaluations**: Line 80-83 in `eval/index.js` gracefully skips missing metrics with a `continue`. This shouldn't happen if CLI validation runs first, but provides defensive handling.

- **Default parameter for thresholds**: `generateReport()` has `thresholds = {}` default (line 67), so `undefined` passed from CLI (line 580) becomes `{}`, ensuring backward compatibility.

### Report Structure Edge Cases

- **Backward compatibility**: Lines 111-114 in `eval/index.js` only add `passed` and `thresholds` fields if thresholds were provided. Reports without thresholds have no these fields, preserving backward compatibility. Tested on lines 144-157 of `index.test.js`.

- **Empty thresholds object**: Passing `thresholds: {}` behaves identically to not providing thresholds—no `passed` or `thresholds` fields in report. This is correct.

### Exit Code Conditions

- **Exit code only checked when thresholds provided**: Lines 590-596 in `index.ts` only check `report.passed` if thresholds were supplied. Without thresholds, the function doesn't exit explicitly (falls through), relying on normal process exit. This could mask errors; consider explicit `process.exit(0)` for clarity.

- **Report written before exit code check**: Report is written (lines 582-586) before threshold exit code evaluation (lines 590-596), so all reports are written regardless of pass/fail. Correct per spec.

- **Markdown threshold rendering**: Line 47 in `reporters.js` displays `threshold.score !== null ? threshold.score : 'n/a'`. - **Thresholds parameter default**: Line 67 in `eval/index.js` uses `thresholds = {}`. If `undefined` is passed, this default is used. If `null` is passed, it remains null, and `Object.keys(null)` will crash. No defensive check for `null`.

- **Commander.js accumulation**: Line 815 in `index.ts` uses commander's built-in accumulation syntax `(value, previous = []) => [...previous, value]`. This correctly handles multiple `--threshold` arguments. No issues found.

---

## Summary

**High Priority:**
1. Hardcoded metric ID list in parse-error message doesn't reflect custom metrics (line 554)
2. Duplicate thresholds silently overwrite without warning (line 517)

**Medium Priority:**
3. Markdown rendering should use `?? 'n/a'` for score display to handle undefined safely (line 47 in reporters.js)
4. Metrics should be validated to have a `label` field before rendering

**Low Priority:**
5. Consider explicit `process.exit(0)` when no thresholds are provided for clarity
6. Add defensive null-check for thresholds parameter in `generateReport()` in case it receives null instead of undefined

14	<intent-contract>
15	
16	## Intent
17	
18	**Problem:** Currently `frai eval` always exits with code 0, preventing CI pipelines from gating on metric thresholds. SDK users using `generateReport` also lack threshold support.
19	
20	**Approach:** Add a `--threshold <metric>=<min>` CLI option (repeatable) to `frai eval` that validates metric scores against minimum values and exits with code 1 if any fail. Implement the threshold logic in `generateReport` (frai-core) to support both CLI and SDK users. Report the outcomes in JSON and Markdown formats.
21	
22	## Boundaries & Constraints
23	
24	**Always:**
25	- Metrics with no score (e.g., `exact_match` when references are missing) fail their threshold rather than crashing or passing.
26	- Exit 0 when all thresholds pass, exit 1 when any fail, exit 2 for usage errors.
27	- Usage errors (malformed threshold syntax, invalid min value, or unknown metric) exit with code 2 and list valid metric IDs.
28	- When no `--threshold` is provided, CLI behavior and exit codes remain unchanged (reports and success/failure unaffected).
29	- The report is written in both success and failure cases, and always records the threshold outcomes.
30	- Threshold logic works for custom metrics passed to `runEvaluations` (matched by metric `id` field).
31	
32	**Never:**
33	- Do not change exit behavior when `--threshold` is not specified.
34	- Do not require `--threshold` as a mandatory option.
35	- Do not assume a metric has a score; validate it exists and is not null.
36	
37	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
38	
39	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
40	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
41	| All thresholds pass | `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, scores are 0.9 and 0.95 | Report written, includes `passed: true`, exit 0 | No error |

## Design Notes

**Threshold validation:** Parse and validate thresholds in the CLI layer (`runEvalCommand`) before calling `generateReport`. This allows a fast error exit (code 2) and prevents report generation on usage errors. The core `generateReport` receives pre-validated thresholds as an object (`{ metric_id: min_value }`).

**Null-score handling:** Metrics with `score: null` are treated as failing their threshold. This avoids silent passes (e.g., exact_match without references) and makes the threshold semantics predictable: "score must be >= min" is false when score is null.

**Report structure:** JSON reports gain top-level `passed` and `thresholds` array fields. Markdown adds an optional "## Thresholds" section. The threshold array mirrors the structure of metrics but is separate, allowing flexible reporting without modifying metric objects.

**Custom metric support:** Since metrics are identified by their `id` field, custom metrics work automatically as long as they include an `id` string. Threshold parsing accepts any string as a metric ID; validation happens by matching against evaluated metrics, so unknown IDs are caught and reported with the valid list.

<intent-contract>

## Intent

**Problem:** Currently `frai eval` always exits with code 0, preventing CI pipelines from gating on metric thresholds. SDK users using `generateReport` also lack threshold support.

**Approach:** Add a `--threshold <metric>=<min>` CLI option (repeatable) to `frai eval` that validates metric scores against minimum values and exits with code 1 if any fail. Implement the threshold logic in `generateReport` (frai-core) to support both CLI and SDK users. Report the outcomes in JSON and Markdown formats.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Metrics with no score (e.g., `exact_match` when references are missing) fail their threshold rather than crashing or passing.
- Exit 0 when all thresholds pass, exit 1 when any fail, exit 2 for usage errors.
- Usage errors (malformed threshold syntax, invalid min value, or unknown metric) exit with code 2 and list valid metric IDs.
- When no `--threshold` is provided, CLI behavior and exit codes remain unchanged (reports and success/failure unaffected).
- The report is written in both success and failure cases, and always records the threshold outcomes.
- Threshold logic works for custom metrics passed to `runEvaluations` (matched by metric `id` field).

**Never:**
- Do not change exit behavior when `--threshold` is not specified.
- Do not require `--threshold` as a mandatory option.
- Do not assume a metric has a score; validate it exists and is not null.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| All thresholds pass | `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, scores are 0.9 and 0.95 | Report written, includes `passed: true`, exit 0 | No error |
| Some thresholds fail | `--threshold exact_match=0.9`, score is 0.8 | Report written, includes `passed: false`, exit 1 | Error: threshold failed |
| Metric has no score | `--threshold exact_match=0.5`, references missing, score is null | Report written, threshold fails, exit 1 | Threshold fails on null |
| Unknown metric | `--threshold unknown_metric=0.5` | No report written, error message lists valid IDs, exit 2 | Usage error |
| Malformed threshold | `--threshold exact_match`, missing `=` | No report written, error message explaining format, exit 2 | Usage error |
| Invalid min value | `--threshold exact_match=1.5` (outside 0-1) | No report written, error message, exit 2 | Usage error |
| No `--threshold` option | Standard eval run | Report written as before, exit 0 always | No error |
| Custom metric with threshold | Custom metric registered, `--threshold custom_id=0.7`, score is 0.8 | Report written, threshold passes, exit 0 | Works for custom metrics |

</intent-contract>

## Code Map

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:476–497` — `runEvalCommand()` function; parses options and calls `Eval.*`; entry point for CLI threshold parsing
- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:51–56` — `EvalOptions` interface; must add `threshold?: string[]` field for repeated `--threshold` args
- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts:709–717` — `program.command('eval')` definition; must add `.option('--threshold', ...)` and pass parsed thresholds to `runEvalCommand`
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:16–39` — `loadDataset()` function; no changes needed (loads outputs/references)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:41–60` — `runEvaluations()` function; no changes needed (runs metrics, returns evaluations array)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:62–82` — `generateReport()` function; must accept optional `thresholds` object (`{ metric_id: min_value }`), evaluate thresholds against evaluations, add `passed` and `thresholds` fields to report
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js:84–94` — `writeReport()` function; no changes needed (delegates formatting to reporters)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js:3–5` — `toJson()` function; passes through JSON; no changes (new `passed` and `thresholds` fields auto-serialize)
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js:7–41` — `toMarkdown()` function; must add "## Thresholds" section showing PASS/FAIL for each threshold
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:21–54` — `exactMatchMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'exact_match'`, `score: null` when references missing; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:56–89` — `toxicityMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'toxicity'`, always has a score; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:91–127` — `lengthVarianceMetric()` returns metric with `id: 'length_variance'`, always has a score; anchor for threshold evaluation logic
- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js:129–133` — `DEFAULT_METRICS` array; needed to enumerate valid metric IDs for error messages

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Add `threshold?: string[]` field to `EvalOptions` interface and `.option('--threshold <metric>=<min>', ...)` to the eval command definition with `action()` accumulating repeated values into an array. Update `runEvalCommand()` to parse and validate thresholds, translate string format to object, and pass to `Eval.generateReport` -- Separates CLI parsing from core logic; enables both synchronous validation and SDK reuse.

- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` -- Modify `generateReport()` to accept optional `thresholds` parameter, implement threshold evaluation logic (match metric by id, check score is not null, compare to min, record pass/fail), add `passed` boolean and `thresholds` array to returned report object -- Core logic is agnostic to CLI; reusable by SDK callers.

- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js` -- Update `toMarkdown()` to add "## Thresholds" section (if thresholds present in report) showing one line per threshold with metric name, min, score, and PASS/FAIL status -- User-visible threshold reporting in markdown format.

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Update `runEvalCommand()` to check `report.passed` and `process.exit(0)` if true or `process.exit(1)` if false; add usage-error handler for malformed thresholds and unknown metrics that calls `process.exit(2)` and logs the error + valid metric IDs -- Enforces exit codes and CLI error messaging.

- `packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js` -- Add test cases: (1) all thresholds pass, report has `passed: true`, (2) some thresholds fail, report has `passed: false`, (3) metric with null score fails its threshold, (4) verify JSON report includes `passed` and `thresholds` fields -- Validates threshold evaluation logic in core.

- `packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` -- Add test cases for CLI threshold parsing: (1) valid `--threshold exact_match=0.8`, (2) multiple thresholds, (3) malformed threshold (no `=`), (4) invalid min (outside 0–1), (5) unknown metric ID, (6) no threshold (backward compatibility) -- Validates CLI parsing and error handling.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

- Given a threshold passed as `--threshold exact_match=0.8` with evaluated exact_match score of 0.9, when `frai eval` runs, then the report includes a thresholds entry with `metric: 'exact_match'`, `min: 0.8`, `score: 0.9`, `passed: true`, and CLI exits 0.
- Given a threshold `--threshold exact_match=0.9` with evaluated exact_match score of 0.8, when `frai eval` runs, then the report has `passed: false`, a thresholds entry shows `passed: false`, and CLI exits 1.
- Given exact_match metric returning `score: null` (no references provided) and threshold `--threshold exact_match=0.5`, when `frai eval` runs, then the thresholds entry shows `passed: false` (null score is not >= min) and CLI exits 1.
- Given threshold `--threshold unknown_metric=0.5`, when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message lists the valid metric IDs (exact_match, toxicity, length_variance, and any custom ones), and CLI exits 2.
- Given threshold `--threshold exact_match` (malformed, no `=` or min), when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message explains the format `<metric>=<number>`, and CLI exits 2.
- Given threshold `--threshold exact_match=1.5` (min outside 0–1), when `frai eval` runs, then no report is written, error message says min must be between 0 and 1, and CLI exits 2.
- Given no `--threshold` option, when `frai eval` runs, then the report has no `passed` or `thresholds` fields, and CLI exits 0 (backward compatible).
- Given markdown format with thresholds `--threshold exact_match=0.8 --threshold toxicity=0.9`, when `frai eval` runs, then the markdown report includes a "## Thresholds" section with two rows showing metric name, min, score, and PASS or FAIL.
- Given `generateReport()` called from SDK with `thresholds: { exact_match: 0.8 }`, when the exact_match metric score is 0.9, then the returned report includes `passed: true` and a thresholds array.

## Design Notes

**Threshold validation:** Parse and validate thresholds in the CLI layer (`runEvalCommand`) before calling `generateReport`. This allows a fast error exit (code 2) and prevents report generation on usage errors. The core `generateReport` receives pre-validated thresholds as an object (`{ metric_id: min_value }`).

**Null-score handling:** Metrics with `score: null` are treated as failing their threshold. This avoids silent passes (e.g., exact_match without references) and makes the threshold semantics predictable: "score must be >= min" is false when score is null.

**Report structure:** JSON reports gain top-level `passed` and `thresholds` array fields. Markdown adds an optional "## Thresholds" section. The threshold array mirrors the structure of metrics but is separate, allowing flexible reporting without modifying metric objects.

**Custom metric support:** Since metrics are identified by their `id` field, custom metrics work automatically as long as they include an `id` string. Threshold parsing accepts any string as a metric ID; validation happens by matching against evaluated metrics, so unknown IDs are caught and reported with the valid list.
